title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the end of a technical stretch of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes (Grothendieck's own numbering is about 648, following p. 647). Over pp. 620–647 he studies groups M_{ρ,σ} and their subgroups. As I read them, these are groups of automorphisms or 'twisted' loops attached to two base points or cusps ρ, σ in a profinite (anabelian) setting.

The objects in play:
- an extension 1→μ_ρ→M^?→M→1;
- a subgroup M^G (written ♮ in the transcription, apparently a decorated 'G'), equal to G^G_{ρ,σ};
- normaliser-type subgroups N_{ρ0}, N_{σ0} (the notation N(σ0) suggests normalisers, e.g. of inertia or decomposition groups at the points ρ0, σ0);
- a quotient Γ0 = Γ_{ρ0,σ0} receiving a map M^G→Γ0.

By (127), the group M^{G?}_{ρ0,σ0} is a fibre product N^{G?}_{ρ0} ×_{Γ0^G} Z^{G!}_{σ0} ×_{Γ0^G} M^G.

The page argues as follows:
1. A certain map (xx) is identified with the third projection of this fibre product.
2. Its image is therefore the inverse image in M^G, under M^G→Γ0, of the image of N^{G?}_{ρ0} ×_{Γ0^G} N^{G!}_{σ0} → Γ0^G ⊂ Γ0.
3. The aim (from p. 647, statement (**)) is that M^?_{ρ0,σ0}→M^G is an epimorphism. It therefore suffices that both N^{G?}_{ρ0}→Γ0^G and N^{G!}_{σ0}→Γ0^G are surjective, since the image of a fibre product over B in B is the intersection of the two images.
4. The first surjectivity is justified by an extension of Γ0^G by some group (H_ρ?); the second by an earlier reference ('12..').
5. He starts a direct check: take u∈Γ0^G coming from u0∈M^G satisfying conditions a)–d) of (107). One finds β0∈G_0^G⊂M^G with β0^{-1}u0∈N(σ0).

The argument then stops. A later marginal note says the verifications were omitted, intending to come back to them. It proved not urgent: it mattered more to develop the special cases ('tame' or 'formal/formalised') to clarify the general structure of the M_{ρ,σ}. The next page switches to a general 'digression de formalisme des groupes': reconstructing (G, normal subgroup 𝔊, N with N/SN ≅ G/𝔊) from (𝔊, N, action N→Aut𝔊, SN→𝔊). This is the classical description of a group as an amalgam / crossed-module-type gluing.
errors: The proof is explicitly incomplete: the surjectivity of N^{G?}_{ρ0}→Γ0^G and N^{G!}_{σ0}→Γ0^G is only sketched, and the final step is broken off. Grothendieck himself notes the verifications were omitted.
Minor notational inconsistency: β0 is introduced but β^{-1}u0 is written. The superscripts on N_{σ0} (! vs ?) differ between this page and the previous one.
On p. 647 he had first written that the epimorphism holds 'contrairement à ce qu'on imaginait'. The page's logic is consistent with that claim, but it remains unproved.

ideas.what: Reducing surjectivity of a map from an iterated fibre product of groups to surjectivity of the factor maps onto the common base
ideas.modern_name: elementary fibre products of groups; image of a fibre product

ideas.what: Study of the groups M_{ρ,σ} (twisted normaliser/loop groups at two base points) and their behaviour under passage to subgroups, as part of the 'loop equation' programme for Galois–Teichmüller theory
ideas.modern_name: normalisers of inertia/decomposition subgroups in profinite fundamental groupoids; Galois–Teichmüller theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, La Longue Marche); later Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps
ideas.where_published: Themes in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated); this specific computation unsure

ideas.what: Methodological decision to treat 'tame' (modéré) and formal special cases first to understand the structure of M_{ρ,σ}
ideas.modern_name: tame fundamental groups / formal (completed, pro-nilpotent-type) versions of the loop equations

missed.claim: The proof that M^?_{ρ0,σ0}→M^G is an epimorphism (reduced to surjectivity of N^{G?}_{ρ0}→Γ0^G and N^{G!}_{σ0}→Γ0^G) was abandoned with verifications omitted. Grothendieck redirected effort to the tame/formal cases.
missed.quote: Ici j'ai omis les vérifications, pensant y revenir dans les jours suivants, il s'avère que ce n'est pas urgent
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor technical lemma in an unpublished development. Its interest is mainly documentary: it shows where the general theory of the M_{ρ,σ} was left and that the tame/formal cases were seen as the key test bed.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine fibre-product surjectivity reduction inside an idiosyncratic, unpublished computation, with an explicit admission of omitted checks. Historically mildly interesting for the redirection toward tame/formal cases, but nothing a specialist would find new or striking.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: 'dans M^G par M^G → Γ0 = Γ_{ρ0,σ0}' (with a struck-out symbol before ρ0) is correct. The superscript rendered 'G' is the same decorated symbol transcribed as ♮ on p. 647.
Fibre product line: N_{ρ0}^{G?} ×_{Γ0^G} N_{σ0}^{G}! → Γ0^G (⊂ Γ0). The index under × is Γ0^G (over-written), with deleted text above.
'Il reste donc à montrer que (xx) est surjectif, ou encore que les deux ...' rather than 'que les deux surjectif'.
'(la première se voit sur l'ext[ension] de Γ0^G par μ_ρ?/H_ρ, la deuxième car (12?))' — the reading is uncertain.
'u ∈ Γ0^G, [-défini par un-] provenant de u0 ∈ M^G = G^G_{ρ,σ}'; then 'satisfaisant donc aux conditions a) b) c) d) de (107)'.
'β0 ∈ G_0^G ⊂ M^G tel que β^{-1}u0 ∈ N(σ0)' — subscript and prime partly unclear.

Bottom note: '...dans les jours suivants, il s'avère que ce n'est pas urgent – il importait plutôt de développer les cas particuliers "tame" ou "formels"(?) pour préciser les idées [sur les?] ... des M_{ρ,σ} ...' — the final line is largely illegible.
